en: Dependent on a state that is with applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicāra*) and not a root (*nahetu*), there arises a state with applied thought and sustained thought that is a root, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. [In the root condition: fifteen;
in the object condition, fifteen; in the predominance condition, fourteen … pe … in the prenascence and repetition conditions, fourteen … pe … in the non-disappearance condition, fifteen.
Dependent on a state that is not accompanied by rapture (*napītisahagata*) and not a root, there arises a state accompanied by rapture that is a root, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of the root condition (*hetu*), there are twenty-eight … [and so on] … in the case of non-disappearance (*avigata*), there are twenty-eight.

Dependent on a state that is not to be abandoned by insight (*na-dassanena-pahātabba*) and is not a root (*nahetu*), a state that is to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanāya-pahātabba*) and is a root arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.
In the case of the root condition, there are nine … [and so on] … in the case of resultant (*vipāka*), there are three … [and so on] … in the case of non-disappearance, there are nine.

Dependent on a state that has roots to be abandoned by vision and is itself rootless, there arises a state with roots to be abandoned by cultivation and which has roots, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. [In the root-condition: nine;
in the object-condition, fourteen; in the predominance-condition, nine ... pe ... in the result-condition, three ... pe ... in the non-disappearance-condition, fourteen.
Dependent on a state that does not lead to accumulation and is rootless, there arises a state leading to dispersal and having roots, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of root-cause condition (*hetu-paccaya*), there are nine; ... pe ... in the case of resultant condition (*vipāka-paccaya*), three; ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance condition (*avigata-paccaya*), nine.
Dependent on a state that is neither-learner-nor-root-cause (*na-sekkha-na-hetu*), a learner-root-cause state arises by way of root-cause condition.

(Abbreviated. In the case of root-cause condition, there are nine; ... pe ... in the case of repetition condition (*āsevana-paccaya*), six; ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance condition, nine.
